chunks: And regarding the ribs, those that are adjacent to the heart: if a rib from them breaks, its wergild is twenty-five dinars; and regarding its fracture (crack), twelve dinars and a half; and the wergild of the displacement of its bone is seven dinars and a half; and its exposure is one-quarter of its breaking, and its piercing is like that; and regarding the ribs from what follows the two upper arms, the wergild of each rib is ten dinars when it breaks; and the wergild of its fracture is seven dinars; and the wergild of the displacement of its bone is five dinars; and the exposure of each rib from them is one-quarter of the wergild of its breaking, being two dinars and a half.

So if a rib from it were pierced, its wergild is two dinars and a half; and regarding the fatal injury (al-jaa'ifah), it is one-third of the wergild of the soul, three hundred and thirty-three dinars and one-third of a dinar. So if it penetrates from both sides, by an arrow or a jab, its wergild is four hundred and thirty-three dinars and one-third of a dinar.

key_terms.الْجَائِفَة: A fatal injury that reaches the vital interior
key_terms.صَدْع: Fracture or crack (as opposed to a complete break)

ai.seo_question: What is the financial compensation for breaking or piercing a rib according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage from al-Kafi outlines the precise monetary compensation (diyah) for rib injuries, reflecting the systematic legal methodology (usul al-fiqh) of the Imams in quantifying bodily damages. It distinguishes between minor fractures and fatal injuries (al-jaa'ifah), which are valued at one-third of the full blood money, a standard derived from the principle that a rib injury is considered a partial wound to the body's core. This detailed classification underscores the Shia emphasis on equitable restitution based on the severity and location of the injury.
